passages.exact_passage: In the high-threshold approximation, excess peak height fixes a radius, and converting that radius into length, area, or volume gives powers 2, 1, and 2/3 in $U=\beta s^{2/d}$. The round regions are a guide reconstruction of the limiting geometry, not observed field shapes; see Mainali et al. (2025), Equation 1 and Supplemental Methods S4, with the parabola constants checked in this chapter.
passages.necessity: Explains the geometric powers while retaining the high-threshold limit and original-guide/source distinction. Its formula now has proper math markup.

passages.exact_passage: A local parabola stands epsilon above threshold q, and its full width is twice r star. U equals q times epsilon and r star is approximately square root of two times sigma divided by q times square root of U. The same radius gives an interval of length 2 r star, a disk of area pi r star squared, or a ball of volume four pi r star cubed over three. Therefore U depends on size to powers 2, 1, and 2/3.
passages.necessity: States peak excess, full width, the corrected radius and three dimensional sizes.
